song.title: Take Me To The River (Bass Only)

guitar.notes: Teenie Hodges was the Hi Records house guitarist on Al Green's classic recordings, known for a clean semi-hollow tone; not as iconically singular as Lucille/Les Paul but well documented in soul/R&B history.

tone.summary: A clean, round tone utilizing compression and a vintage American amp model (US Deluxe) paired with a 2x12 cabinet to simulate the warm, foundational role of the missing bass element.

rig.name: Al Green - Take Me To The River (Bass Only) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up any low-frequency hum or rumble from the source material.
Smooth out the dynamics and add sustain, mimicking the consistent output of a bass instrument.
blocks.gap: The Comp module is designed for guitar strings; it will compress low frequencies aggressively. This is the best available tool to achieve smooth, foundational tone.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone clean and foundational, avoiding any grit or distortion that would clash with a bass role.
Provide a warm, round, and articulate clean tone suitable for simulating the low-end warmth of a bass line.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is primarily designed for mid-range clarity. We are maximizing its bass response to compensate for the lack of dedicated bass amp modeling.

blocks.purpose: Select a smaller cabinet to maintain clarity and focus the low-mids, preventing excessive boominess.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is generally suited for rhythm guitar. We are using it here to provide a focused, non-boomy voicing that complements the clean amp choice.

blocks.purpose: Boost the fundamental low frequencies (sub-bass) and slightly tame the upper mids to create a deep, warm foundation.
blocks.gap: This is a general EQ module. We are using it specifically as a parametric equalizer to sculpt the bass response curve.

blocks.purpose: No modulation needed. Keeping the signal dry and direct to maintain rhythmic punch.
Add a subtle sense of space and glue the sound together without muddying the low end.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is suitable for adding warmth, but care must be taken not to let the decay time become too long and obscure the bass fundamentals.

blocks.purpose: No delay needed. Keeping the rhythm direct and punchy.

improvements.summary: Replace the generic cabinet simulation with an IR optimized for deep, warm bass tones to improve low-end realism.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Bass focused IR (e.g., Ampeg 4x10 or dedicated sub)
proposals.reason: The US 2x12 is too bright and lacks the necessary girth for a bass role.
proposals.expectedGain: Deeper, warmer low end; less upper-mid focus.
